title.narrative: Supporting Yemen’s Low Emissions Development through the preparation of the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), while enhancing required capacities and project pipeline in support of reducing emissions.

description.narrative:
There are several on-going and completed initiatives (see 1.11 and Table 2), financed by the GCF and other sources that have targeted some of these readiness capacity gaps. The proposed readiness project builds on these initiatives to further improve the current baseline readiness capacities by addressing the remaining gaps in the intersectoral coordination and strategic priority and direction setting for climate change mitigation, mapping of readiness capacity needs and development of bankable projects.
The goal of the proposed project is to ensure enabling conditions for the Government of Yemen and its key actors to effectively implement its priority actions for reducing its GHG emissions in line with the Paris Agreement. The project will achieve this goal based on its transformational logic as follows: IF the project clarifies roles and responsibilities among the LED Network members and improves knowledge and engagement of the LED network members on mitigation, identifies long-term readiness needs for climate change mitigation, updates Yemen’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), and develops a good quality concept note on climate change mitigation that aims at operationalizing the NDC, THEN Yemen’s enabling conditions for climate change mitigation will be strengthened significantly BECAUSE key stakeholders, including the private sector local government and urban representatives, will be actively engaged in planning, implementing, and monitoring climate change mitigation initiatives, guided by government’s continued commitment and leadership in addressing climate change, the country’s updated international commitment, and the increased international support in term of climate finance and technical assistance. A multi-level governance / planning approach will be used.
To achieve this goal, the project will remove the following critical barriers through the delivery of five GCF Readiness Outcomes and project specific outputs. - Lack of capacity and resources to operationalize dedicated institutional arrangements for effective intersectoral dialogue and coordination. - Limited private sector interest and engagement in climate change mitigation activities due to a lack of plans and strategies to incentivize investment by the sector. - Limited technical expertise available in the country to set clear mitigation policy directions and priority actions and identify gaps in enabling conditions. - Limited national expertise and resources for mitigation actions due to competing priorities. Under Readiness Outcome 1.1, the project will operationalize and strengthen the capacity of Yemen’s Low Emissions Development (LED) Committee in intersectoral dialogue and coordination and knowledge management.
Under Readiness Outcome 1.3, the project will develop a mechanism and plan of action to increase private sector engagement in LED sectors by identifying the private sector needs and common ground. Under Readiness Outcome 2.1, the project will identify the country’s readiness capacity needs for mitigation sectors by providing the necessary technical expertise. Under Readiness Outcome 2.2, the Page 5 of 36 project will update the country’s NDC by providing the necessary technical expertise and supporting intersectoral discussions. Under Readiness Outcome 4.3, the project will develop a bankable project concept note for climate change mitigation to increase Yemen’s access to international climate finance by providing project initiation expertise and resources.
The primary beneficiary of the proposed project is the Government of Yemen and key actors in the sectors relevant to climate change mitigation. More specifically, the project will support the NDA/EPA, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation, LED Network/Committee members, including the private sector, local banks, Accredited Entities (AEs), future Direct Access Entities (DAEs), potential Executing Entities (EEs), and Delivery Partners (DPs).
Added value for UN-Habitat: Calculations of GHG emissions from Urban areas / settlements will be made based on GHG emission inventories to coming out from the BUR2. Based on that, a social and economic impacts assessment of possible GHG reduction actions as identified in the NDC will be conducted, including impacts on urban areas / settlements. Based on that a NDC financing strategy will be developed, highlighted needs in urban areas / settlements.
